description: Machine-readable expected outcome for every fixture in this directory. `verify-fixtures.mjs` reads this file and fails (non-zero exit) if any fixture's actual outcome does not match. `expected` is one of "accept" | "reject" | "ignore". For "reject" fixtures, `reason_code` must be present among the detected failure reasons (there may be more than one, e.g. a personal-dimension violation is also caught independently by schema validation, since every object in this protocol's schemas already declares additionalProperties:false).

fixtures.notes: Smallest well-formed token-usage/v1 payload: one record, complete coverage, wrapped in a valid envelope.
Multiple records across two agents/models/token_kinds, partial coverage with one omission. Exercises that cache_write_1h and cache_read are kept distinct, not collapsed.
data.mode=snapshot with records=[] and coverage.status=no_data is a valid, honest snapshot -- absence of measurable data is representable, not an error.

Same {schema, repository, subject} identity, different generated_at/head_sha/token counts (a re-measurement). Both payloads are individually valid, share the same recomputed upsert_key, and the second's content differs from the first -- in a real store the second upserts over the first rather than creating a second row.

The correction (second payload) drops a record present in the first entirely, rather than zeroing it out, and adjusts coverage accordingly. Verifies snapshot-replace semantics are representable without a tombstone/delete record: the full replacement is the only signal a harvester needs.
sha256 field does not match the sha256 of the base64-decoded payload bytes -- must be rejected before the payload is even parsed as JSON.
payload_b64 field is not valid RFC 4648 base64.

Declared upsert_key is well-formed (matches am1_[0-9a-f]{64}) but does not match recomputing the RFC 8785 JCS recipe over {schema, repository, subject}. A harvester MUST recompute, never trust the declared value.

A forbidden personal-dimension key ("reviewer") appears nested inside a token-usage record, not just at the top level. Caught independently by both the dedicated personal-dimension scan and, in this fixture, also by additionalProperties:false schema validation -- the two are meant to be redundant (defense in depth), not mutually exclusive.

schema="review-result/v1" is well-formed at the envelope level but is not a kind this v1 token-usage harvester understands. MUST be routed to a rejection log without attempting partial interpretation of `data` -- never guessed at.

An HTML comment using a different tag entirely (not "agent-metrics:v1"). MUST be silently skipped, not treated as a malformed agent-metrics marker -- this is what lets other tools keep posting their own hidden comments on the same PR without collision.
